{'content': 'I mentioned in an article about Siri AI and Apple Watch earlier today that before watchOS 27 officially launches this month, I still hope Apple will revert one thing. This is a feature I have used for many years that has become muscle memory, and I have felt uncomfortable about it disappearing all summer.'}

{'content': 'In watchOS 27, double-clicking the Digital Crown can no longer quickly switch between different apps.'}

{'content': 'In the article I wrote this morning, I mentioned:'}

{'content': 'When Apple released the first public beta of watchOS 27 in July, I had already pointed out this issue, and I had also conveyed my feedback to Apple back in June.'}

{'content': 'For many years, Apple Watch has had a built-in hidden gesture feature that allows you to quickly switch between two apps, or jump between recently used apps and the watch face.'}

{'content': 'This is an operation I have not consciously thought about for years, but I have actually been using it all along.'}

{'content': 'In watchOS 27, whether you single-click or double-click the Digital Crown, it brings up the dynamic app list.'}

{'content': 'The first beta of watchOS 27 removed this feature, and the reason appears to be that Apple wants to heavily promote the brand new "dynamic app list" feature in watchOS 27. Now, pressing the Digital Crown displays the Siri app icon, plus five smart-recommended app icons, and an icon that lets you see all apps.'}

{'content': 'The dynamic app list actually becomes more intuitive the more you use it. If the app you want is already in the recommended dock, it is very convenient.'}

{'content': 'But it can never fully replace the reliable and direct operation of double-clicking to switch apps. There is simply no way to do this in watchOS 27. In the watchOS 27 beta, double-clicking the Digital Crown has the same effect as single-clicking the button.'}

{'content': 'The old method allowed you to quickly jump back and forth between apps like Workout and Music.'}

{'content': 'I have mentioned before that the physical buttons on Apple Watch are already very limited, with only the Ultra model featuring an Action button. Considering this, I think removing the double-click gesture on the Digital Crown was a wrong decision.'}

{'content': 'The double-click function of the side button below the Digital Crown is still preserved, which is used to open the cards in Apple Wallet. I hope the official version of watchOS 27 can restore the same gesture for the Digital Crown button, or at least watchOS 27.1.'}

{'content': 'Do you use this gesture on Apple Watch? Have you felt inconvenienced in the watchOS 27 beta? Will you miss it after upgrading? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.'}
